L1.hi: विश्वामित्र जाने को मुड़ चुके थे।

L3.en: He told the king: a man of this house keeps his word.
L3.hi: उन्होंने राजा को बताया — इस घर का आदमी वचन निभाता है।
L3.te: రాజుకి చెప్పాడు — ఈ ఇంటి మనిషి మాట తప్పడు.
L3.speaker: VASISHTHA
L3.speaker_rule: VASISHTHA's statement, not narrator fact. Attributed in every language.

L4.en: Then he told him: the sage he refused was Rāma's protection.
L4.hi: फिर बताया — जिस ऋषि को वो मना कर रहे थे, वही राम की रक्षा थे।
L4.te: తర్వాత చెప్పాడు — ఎవరిని కాదంటున్నాడో, ఆ ఋషే రాముడికి రక్ష.
L4.speaker: VASISHTHA
L4.speaker_rule: VASISHTHA's statement, not narrator fact. Attributed in every language.

screenplay.en: He told the king: a man of this house keeps his word.
Then he told him: the sage he refused was Rāma's protection.

Room tone, unchanged from film 5 — same hall, same lamps. **The score returns once**, two
notes under beats 13 and 14, and is gone before he calls. Feet and cloth as the court moves
at beat 16. The doorway hold is room tone only, with the faint sound of the hall being
larger than it was.

share_cut.connect_line: Can anyone change the king’s mind?

continuity._what: What must not change between cuts.
standing_rules: The lamp stays where it is. Its flame moves; its position does not.
Daśaratha's ring is on the right hand in every hand detail, in every film.
The throne is occupied in films 1–2 and empty from film 3 onward. It is never re-occupied.
Viśvāmitra's staff is planted at his right through films 1–4. It moves once, in film 5.
The sage's cloth and seated posture do not change across four films — that stillness is the performance and a shifted fold breaks it.
Once the king steps down in film 3, he does not return to the dais in any later shot.

per_join.continuous: The frame is IDENTICAL across the join — same plate, same grade, same room tone. Not a similar frame: the same one.
per_join.hard: Location or time has changed. Room tone changes with it.

never: Do not play the king as defeated. Both sources have him well-pleased within. He is being
Do not let Vasiṣṭha raise his voice, gesture, or lecture. He stands and states.
Do not have the sage soften, thank, or nod in satisfaction. He turns back. That is all.
Do not put a musical resolution under the giving. The chord resolves at 13–14, *before*
Do not end on the king. End on the door.
